title: Eliminate chronic subjective tinnitus after a finite treatment

concept.text: Produce sustained disappearance of chronic tinnitus percepts after treatment ends. Existing management can reduce distress and severity; neither NIH nor WHO identifies a definitive cure. Proposed completion test: Regulatory authorization supported by an adequately powered sham-controlled trial in chronic subjective tinnitus, showing a significantly higher complete-remission rate than control, maintained for at least 12 months after treatment ends, with no continuing masking or stimulation. Test set by: Proposed editorial test; no externally standardized cure threshold was identified. WHO distinguishes the tinnitus percept from tinnitus disorder and associated suffering. Overlaps: PSY-07. Sources given: [NIDCD tinnitus evidence and treatment overview](https://www.nidcd.nih.gov/health/tinnitus) ; [WHO tinnitus questions and answers](https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/deafness-and-hearing-loss--tinnitus).

page.title: Treatment-free remission of chronic subjective tinnitus
page.definition: A finite treatment causes sustained disappearance of tinnitus: sound heard only by the affected person without an external source, persisting for more than 3 months. The sound remains absent after treatment ends, including in silence while deliberately listening for it.

goal.need: An estimated 9.8% of adults have chronic tinnitus (95% CI, 4.7%–19.3%). For some, the sound disrupts sleep or concentration. Background sound can mask it, and cognitive behavioral therapy can ease the distress it causes. Someone whose tinnitus subsided after treatment could fall asleep in quiet or concentrate without the sound intruding. That benefit lasts while the sound stays away. Tinnitus can recur even after more than six months of silence.

completion.title: A finite treatment increases total tinnitus remission lasting over 6 months after treatment ends.
completion.criterion: In adults with subjective tinnitus lasting more than 3 months, a finite treatment produces a statistically higher rate than sham/placebo of total remission lasting more than 6 months after tinnitus-directed treatment ends. Total remission means no tinnitus perception even in silence with deliberate attention, without masking or continuing stimulation. A preregistered, adequately powered, blinded randomized trial meets its prespecified superiority test and documents adverse events.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis. No outside body was found to define the full test of treatment-free remission.
completion.basis: Sanchez and colleagues used more than six months of perceptual silence to identify people already in remission. The Regensburg consensus recommends validated questionnaires, and the international trial-methodology proposal recommends choosing the primary outcome to match the intended effect. AAO-HNSF recommends registration, adequate power, randomization, blinding and careful placebo selection. The Atlas combines the case definition with a controlled test of treatment efficacy. FDA’s Lenire indication covers temporary symptom relief.

milestones.title: Noise-exposed rats recover gap detection through 3 weeks after treatment ends.
milestones.criterion: In noise-exposed rats with impaired gap detection, pair tones with vagus-nerve stimulation for 18 days. Test whether a silent gap in background sound reduces the startle response compared with trials without a gap (P < 0.05), including at the presumed tinnitus frequency. Demonstrate restored gap detection at 1 day, 1 week and 3 weeks after treatment, with sham-treated rats as controls.
milestones.set_by: Engineer et al., University of Texas at Dallas and MicroTransponder; published noise-exposed-rat experimental protocol, not a clinical cure standard.
milestones.threshold_quote: the impairment in gap detection was also eliminated when measured one day, one week and three weeks after the end of the therapy.

milestones.title: Matched tinnitus loudness falls more with paired stimulation than with sound alone over 4 weeks.
milestones.criterion: In a blinded, randomized crossover trial, adults who can alter their tinnitus with head or neck movements receive paired sound and electrical skin stimulation or sound alone for 30 minutes daily for 28 days. Each week they adjust an external sound to match their tinnitus loudness. The reduction from baseline during active treatment exceeds the reduction during sound-only sham (P < 0.05).
milestones.set_by: Marks et al., University of Michigan; published human proof-of-concept protocol, restricted to somatic tinnitus.
milestones.threshold_quote: The active bimodal treatment produced a significant (P<0.05) cumulative decrease in tinnitus loudness

milestones.title: Paired stimulation reduces matched tinnitus loudness beyond control after 6 weeks without treatment.
milestones.criterion: In adults with bothersome somatic tinnitus, compare paired sound and electrical skin stimulation with sound alone for 30 minutes daily for 6 weeks, followed by 6 weeks without treatment. Measure change from baseline in matched tinnitus loudness at weeks 6 and 12, in decibels relative to hearing threshold. In the randomized comparison before crossover, the reduction through week 12 must be greater with paired stimulation (two-sided P < 0.05).
milestones.set_by: University of Michigan protocol NCT03621735, reported by Jones et al.; restricted to bothersome somatic tinnitus.
milestones.threshold_quote: Primary end points were changes in TFI score and tinnitus loudness level from baseline through week 6 and week 12.

milestones.title: People with daily tinnitus for over 3 months have no tinnitus perception for over 6 months.
milestones.criterion: Establish by structured interview that the person previously heard tinnitus daily for more than 3 months and has since had more than 6 months without hearing it, even when deliberately listening in silence. Exclude masking and habituation. The interview establishes remission without attributing it to a treatment.
milestones.set_by: Sanchez, Valim and Schlee, published case-collection inclusion protocol; a study-specific definition of total remission, without a requirement establishing treatment causation.
milestones.threshold_quote: total remission (lack of tinnitus perception, even in silence and with deliberate attention to it) for over 6 months.

milestones.title: A person with chronic tinnitus hears no tinnitus immediately after a 30-second masking sound stops.
milestones.criterion: In the Roberts residual-inhibition test, the participant listens to their tinnitus for 30 seconds, hears a masking sound for 30 seconds, then rates the change in tinnitus loudness. A rating of −5 indicates complete disappearance. After rating the change, the participant signals when tinnitus returns to its usual loudness. The timer stops at 45 seconds.
milestones.set_by: Roberts and colleagues, published human residual-inhibition protocol

not_found: No controlled report located demonstrated superiority for total perceptual remission lasting over six months after a finite treatment ended.
No position opposing pursuit of sustained perceptual remission was located in the tinnitus society, funder or clinical guidance reviewed.

results.finding: In noise-exposed rats (7 treated, 9 sham controls), paired stimulation restored gap detection through 3 weeks after treatment.
results.detail: The main text reports seven treated rats in the behavioral experiment. Figure 2a plots five, and the Methods identify two additional treated rats assessed behaviorally without cortical mapping.
results.quote: In the rats that received VNS paired with multiple tones, the impairment in gap detection was also eliminated when measured one day, one week and three weeks after the end of the therapy.

results.finding: In the post-treatment cohort of 13 noise-exposed guinea pigs, the gap-startle tinnitus index fell with paired stimulation at the treated frequency (frequency-by-group P = 0.0069).
results.detail: The P value is for the frequency-by-group interaction. The paper gives the total post-treatment cohort size but does not specify the number in each arm in the supplied text.
results.quote: Mean TI was significantly reduced in the ET-treat group at the treated frequency (On-Freq; 8 kHz) but not untreated frequencies (Off-Freq; 12 and 16 kHz).

results.finding: In 20 adults with somatic tinnitus, paired stimulation reduced matched loudness by a mean of 8.035 dB from baseline across treatment, significantly more than sound-only sham.
results.detail: The paper reports the active-versus-sham contrast as significant and gives an overall ANOVA P value of 5.5e-5. It does not give a separate exact P value for that pairwise contrast in the supplied text.
results.quote: Tinnitus reduction reached an average of 12.2 dB in the fourth week of active treatment.

results.finding: In 20 adults with somatic tinnitus, the matched-loudness reduction did not persist during the 4-week washout after paired stimulation.
results.detail: The analysis pooled both crossover sequences. Improvement in the Tinnitus Functional Index during washout measures the impact of tinnitus on daily life.
results.quote: Although reduced tinnitus loudness did not carry over into the washout period, this benefit was persistent enough to accumulate over several days of treatment.

results.finding: Two of 20 adults with somatic tinnitus reported complete disappearance near the end of paired stimulation.
results.detail: The disappearance was reported during treatment. Its duration was unspecified.
results.quote: Of the 20 participants tested, two reported complete elimination of their tinnitus towards the end of the active treatment period.

results.finding: Among 99 adults with bothersome somatic tinnitus, paired stimulation reduced matched loudness by 4.5 dB SL more than sound alone at week 12.
results.detail: Treatment effects carried over into the second period, so the investigators analyzed only the first, randomized period.

results.finding: All 80 volunteers with chronic daily tinnitus had been in total remission for more than 6 months.
results.quote: By publishing announcements, we included volunteers of any gender and age who have had daily perception of tinnitus for over 3 months and have been in total remission (lack of tinnitus perception, even in silence and with deliberate attention to it) for over 6 months.

results.finding: In 99 adults with bothersome somatic tinnitus, matched loudness fell 4.5 dB sensation level more with paired stimulation than with sound alone at week 12.
results.detail: The investigators analyzed the first randomized period because the treatment effect persisted through washout and carried over into the second period.
results.quote: and was as much as 11 dB SL greater at week 12 of phase 2 (ITT population: –4.5 dB SL [ P  = .001]; PP population: –7 dB SL [ P  < .001]).

results.finding: In 59 adults with chronic bilateral tinnitus, 3 reported complete suppression throughout residual-inhibition testing.
results.detail: The Discussion explicitly reports complete suppression in three participants. The Results describe those three as having elimination or near-elimination after all maskers and group peak ratings of −5.0 through −4.0 together.

three subjects reported
complete tinnitus suppression for the entire RI test
